title: LTS release gatekeeper and embargoed rollout catalog for Private upgrades
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Scope: build an opinionated release gatekeeper and a metadata-driven rollout catalog for Redwood Private upgrades (VPC / on-prem). This ticket designs and implements the control plane components that enforce LTS pinning, embargo windows, staged cohort schedules, and transactional rollback checkpoints for stateful services. Goals: 1) Prevent accidental cross-channel upgrades by validating customer LTS mapping before rollout; 2) Provide an 'embargo' calendar that blocks upgrades in customer-defined blackout windows (maintenance windows, fiscal dates); 3) Offer a reusable rollout catalog (policy + schedule + health checks) that can be composed into upgrade pipelines and dry-run plans; 4) Emit deterministic telemetry for post-rollout regression detection and billing reconciliation.

Design decisions: the gatekeeper will be a lightweight policy evaluator that runs preflight checks and returns a pass/fail + explanation. Policies will include: LTS-compatibility matrix verification, compatibility label checks (storage schema, kafka wire versions), preflight smoke-run success, and embargo-window check. Rollout catalog entries are small JSON documents (version, cohorts, canary-size, hold-after-timems, health probes, abort-conditions) stored in the control plane and referenced by upgrade jobs. We decided to keep policy evaluation synchronous in the coordinator to simplify failure semantics (trade-off: slightly more latency during job submission vs. easier auditability).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Gatekeeper API (/v1/gatekeeper/validate) that returns structured reasons for block/fail (OK, BLOCKED_BY_EMBARGO, INCOMPAT_LTS, FAILED_PREFLIGHT)
- Rollout catalog UI + API able to create, list, and schedule catalog entries; examples for: quick-canary, silent-canary, staged-wave, and full-cutover
- CLI and API support for dry-run: apply the gatekeeper to a synthetic plan and output expected cohort timings and any failing policy rules
- End-to-end e2e test that runs a private-upgrade job against a disposable VPC cluster and validates canary cutover and abort path
- Telemetry: rollout_id, catalog_id, gatekeeper_decisions, cohort_timings, abort_reason, and checksum of preflight artifacts exported to metrics and traces

Operational notes: 
- Backups: every rollout catalog change is versioned; gatekeeper decisions are immutable and mirrored in the audit log for 90 days by default
- Rollback: introduce a transactional checkpoint that can rewind a subset of services to the previous pinned LTS if critical health probes fail during the hold window
- Performance: policy evaluation must complete <2s in 99th percentile in the control plane; we will add caching of LTS compatibility results per-customer to reduce repeated work.

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/LTS+Gatekeeper+Design ; Example rollout catalog draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-rollout-catalog ; Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1245

Notes on scope exclusions: this ticket does NOT implement the underlying schema migration runner or database delta applier; instead it integrates with the schema-runner service via a defined preflight check interface. Migration orchestration work will be in a follow-up ticket once the gatekeeper contracts are stable.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Triaged by release engineering. Marked P1 due to customer impact for LTS pinning issues reported in Q4 customers.
2026-02-18 - Architecture review: PM request to support embargo windows per-customer and global holidays. Decided to model embargo as calendar ranges with optional timezone per-customer.

2026-02-25 - Design review with infra: decided to keep policy evaluation sync to the coordinator to simplify audit and rollback semantics. Runtime cost accepted because validations run at job submission, not per-token serving.

2026-03-01 - Engineering spike: implemented PoC gatekeeper with two policies (LTS check, embargo) and a simple in-memory catalog. Found edge case: customers with overlapping embargo windows (timezone-aware) — added normalization step to policy evaluation.

2026-03-05 - QA: dry-run harness executed against disposable VPC; discovered flaky health-probe evaluation on scale-down; added transient failure tolerance window to catalog (hold-after-timems) and updated acceptance criteria.

2026-03-10 - PR opened: platform#1245 (gatekeeper API + catalog CRUD + basic UI changes). Requesting @elaine.su for product review and @oana.petrescu for security review (unless flagged minimal surface).

2026-03-12 - Status: merging gatekeeper core API behind feature flag 'lts-gatekeeper'. Next: expand policies to include storage-schema label checks and hook to schema-runner dry-run API. Ops to prepare runbook for emergency abort.
